title: Le Marais
body: The hinge of every trip — falafel on Rue des Rosiers, the arcades at Place des Vosges, the covered market at Enfants Rouges, Pompidou at the edge. Flat, endlessly walkable, shot from every angle across the years.

title: The Islands
body: Île de la Cité and Île Saint-Louis as one slow arc — Notre-Dame, Sainte-Chapelle, Berthillon, and the view west from the bridges at last light.

title: Latin Quarter
body: Medieval lanes into the literary Left Bank — Shakespeare and Company, Rue Mouffetard downhill at lunch, the small streets doing the work.

title: Saint-Germain
body: Café terraces, the Luxembourg chairs, the bouquinistes toward the Pont des Arts — and Orsay holding the riverbank. The Left Bank at reading pace.

title: Louvre & Opéra
body: The dense royal centre — the pyramid courtyard, Tuileries, the Palais-Royal colonnades, the Orangerie. One métro stop wide, a full day deep.

title: Champs-Élysées
body: Skip most of the avenue; keep the two endpoints — Alexandre III with the Grand Palais at sunset, and the Arc rooftop for the best view in Paris.

title: Eiffel & Invalides
body: Trocadéro at the hour the tower goes gold, then the calmer 7e behind it — Rodin’s garden, Invalides, lunch on Rue Cler.

title: Montmartre
body: Not just the summit — the slopes. Rue des Abbesses, the quieter lanes, the Maison Rose, and the steps below Sacré-Cœur facing out over the city.

title: Canal Saint-Martin
body: Flat white in hand along the iron footbridges — locks opening mid-morning, the whole quarter best done as one long walk.

title: Bastille & the East
body: Least touristed, most lived-in — the two markets at Aligre, a glass at the Baron Rouge, and the cobbled avenues of Père-Lachaise under the planes.

title: Montparnasse
body: The bones of the city — literally, in the Catacombs — plus the one skyline view with the Eiffel Tower in it, and the 14e’s quiet market street below.
